thread.title: Rice takes early lead at American Conference Championships after strong performances

author: Houston Republic
title: Rice takes early lead at American Conference Championships after strong performances
text:
Rice University leads after the first day of the American Conference Championships in Greensboro, North Carolina, with a total of 354.5 points. The team secured two event titles on Day 1 and is ahead of Liberty University, which holds second place with 323 points. East Carolina is in third place with 218.5 points.
The finals session began with Rice achieving a season-best time in the 200-yard medley relay. Abigail King, Siiri Einio, Lily Archibald, and Avery Karacz finished third with a time of 1:39.05.
Ava Portello defended her title in the 500 freestyle, finishing first in 4:42.67 and earning an automatic berth to the NCAA championships. Ella Dyson placed third (4:47.28), Ava Hemblett finished fourth (4:47.61), and Sami Johnson came tenth (4:49.70). The team scored a total of 104 points from this event.
In the 200 individual medley, Rice took the top two positions—Reese Cole won with a time of 1:58.28 and freshman Bella Zhang was second at 1:59.06. Lily Cramer added an eighth-place finish (2:01.97). Gio Musiello won the B final (2:01.47) and Abigail King competed in the C final (2:04.17). This event yielded Rice’s highest point total for the day at 107.
For the 50 freestyle, Avery Karacz (23.08), Lizzie Zadel (22.92), and Zara Bolton (23.36) together contributed to a score of 49.5 points for Rice in that event.
In diving, Rice earned an additional 15.1 points by scoring a combined total of 207.50.
Head coach Seth Huston commented on his team’s performance saying, “We had a great first day of the meet; lots of energy and some really great racing,” adding that “Ava Portello earned an automatic NCAA bid with her 500 free victory and led from start to finish.” He also praised his athletes’ approach in another event by stating, “The 1-2 finish in the 200 IM with Reese Cole and Bella Zhang was awesome. They stayed in their lane and executed their race plans to a T.”
